calc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
calc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match).

calc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
calc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

calc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators.
calc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term.

keys_to_translate.ip_main_desc: Test Branch Pressure and Uniformity Estimate

keys_to_translate.ip_is_lateral: Lat. ?
keys_to_translate.ip_count: Emitters ?
keys_to_translate.ip_km: Km ?
keys_to_translate.ip_elev_ds: DS Elev. ?
keys_to_translate.ip_elev_ds_missing_warn: Last emitter elevation (last row) was left blank and defaulted to flat — enter it for an accurate result ⚠
keys_to_translate.ip_hl: Hl ?
keys_to_translate.ip_pressure_warn: Low/negative pressure — check for subatmospheric conditions
keys_to_translate.ip_q_supply: Test path supply flow, Qsupply ?
keys_to_translate.ip_dp_avg: Est. Δpressure, avg. vs. test lateral ?
keys_to_translate.ip_q_avg_field: Est. field-average emitter flow, qavg,field ?
keys_to_translate.ip_du_estimate: Uniformity check, qlast/qavg,field ?
keys_to_translate.ip_worst_case_warn: Test emitter pressure is at or above supply pressure — this path is not likely your worst-case lateral. Check for a more remote or higher-friction lateral, or an elevation profile that better represents the actual worst case.
keys_to_translate.ip_q_ratio: Last emitter flow vs. design flow, qlast/qdesign ?
keys_to_translate.ip_no_solution: No solution: required supply pressure exceeds the entered supply pressure. Increase supply pressure, reduce demand, or use a larger pipe.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_1_def: Guesses the pressure at the last (most remote) emitter, then marches the Energy Grade Line back toward the supply, reach by reach, adding friction and minor losses along the way. Elevation and velocity head are backed out at each node to report the actual pressure there. The guessed far-end pressure is adjusted (bisection) until the computed required supply pressure matches the entered supply pressure — the same closed-loop problem addressed by the pipe-flow solver on the Manning Pipe Flow calculator, extended to a branching network.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_2_def: Each row is one reach along the single hydraulically worst path (the test path) from the supply to the last emitter. A Main reach only passes flow to laterals not on the test path, so its draw is a flat multiplication (design flow × the reach’s total emitter count) — no local pressure sensitivity. The main is a shared trunk pipe, so the reach right at the test lateral’s own takeoff must include not just laterals between its own endpoints but also any laterals still further down the main beyond that takeoff, or sharing the same junction (e.g. an opposite-side lateral) — their flow travels through that same reach before splitting off, whether or not they appear anywhere else in this table. A Lateral reach is a segment of the test lateral itself: emitter discharge is computed from the actual local pressure via q = k·H<sup>x</sup>, and friction loss is reduced by Christiansen’s F(n) factor to account for flow stepping down as each emitter in the reach draws off.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_3_def: Models one fixed inlet pressure (no pump curve), one test path only (not the full field), and a 2-parameter emitter curve (set the exponent near 0 to approximate a pressure-compensating emitter). Two different ratios are reported, deliberately kept separate: q<sub>last</sub>/q<sub>avg,field</sub> is a uniformity check, shaped like textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity (low-group average ÷ population mean) but computed from the test lateral’s own modeled emitters, corrected by an entered Δpressure estimate rather than a full-field statistical sample — the test lateral is deliberately the presumed worst case, so its raw, uncorrected average would understate the true field average and make uniformity look better than it is; the Δpressure input exists specifically to counter that bias. Values at or above 1 are still possible (e.g. the Δpressure estimate is too small, or a favorable downhill run). q<sub>last</sub>/q<sub>design</sub> is a different, non-uniformity check against the manufacturer’s rated flow — useful for spotting an over- or under-pressured system overall, but not a substitute for the uniformity number, since the design/rated flow has no necessary relationship to the system’s actual mean operating pressure.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_4_def: Christiansen, J.E. (1942). “Irrigation by sprinkling.” California Agricultural Experiment Station Bulletin 670. ASAE/ASABE standards for microirrigation design use the same multi-outlet friction-loss approach.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_5_def: Application rate and system/zone flow use the estimated field-average emitter flow (q<sub>avg,field</sub> — the test lateral’s own average, corrected by the entered Δpressure estimate), not a guessed rate: PR = q<sub>avg,field</sub> / A<sub>e</sub>, fed by the corrected modeled value. Spacing and system-wide lateral/emitter counts are separate inputs here because the test path only models one worst-case branch, not every lateral in the field.
keys_to_translate.irr_card_pressure_desc: Model the pressure and flow profile along a main-lateral-emitter branch to estimate distribution uniformity from the real test-path pressure, not just a catalog emitter flow rate.
